_about: The fourteen eras of the Timeline. Modern conservative dating: Exodus 1446 BC, Thiele's king dates, Merrill's for Saul, David and Solomon. Years are signed (negative = BC) and there is no year 0. `book` is the book whose color the band takes; null falls back to the app's neutral color. Judah Alone and the Exile overlap on purpose (605-586).

eras.name: Primeval History
eras.summary: From Creation to the Tower of Babel: the Fall, the Flood and the scattering of the nations. Dates follow the Genesis 5 and 11 genealogies back from Abram, and are approximate.

eras.name: The Patriarchs
eras.summary: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph: God's covenant promises to one family, from Abram's birth to Jacob's move into Egypt.

eras.name: Israel in Egypt
eras.summary: Four hundred and thirty years in Egypt (Exodus 12:40), from honored guests in Goshen to slaves building store cities for Pharaoh.

eras.name: Exodus and Wilderness
eras.summary: The Passover, the Red Sea, the Law at Sinai, the tabernacle, and forty years in the wilderness after the refusal at Kadesh.

eras.name: Conquest
eras.summary: Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan, takes the land and divides it among the tribes.

eras.name: Judges
eras.summary: Cycles of sin, oppression and deliverance, when there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

eras.name: United Kingdom
eras.summary: Saul, David and Solomon reign over all twelve tribes; Jerusalem becomes the capital and the Temple is built.

eras.name: Divided Kingdom
eras.summary: Israel in the north and Judah in the south, side by side, until Assyria destroys Samaria.

eras.name: Judah Alone
eras.summary: Judah survives Assyria under Hezekiah and is reformed under Josiah, until Babylon destroys Jerusalem.

eras.name: Exile
eras.summary: Judah carried to Babylon in three waves, from Daniel in 605 to the fall of Jerusalem in 586, until Cyrus lets them go home.

eras.name: Return and Rebuilding
eras.summary: The return under Zerubbabel, the second Temple, Esther in Persia, and Ezra and Nehemiah rebuilding the people and the walls.

eras.name: Between the Testaments
eras.summary: Four hundred years with no new prophet: Persia, Alexander, the Ptolemies and Seleucids, the Maccabees, and Rome. Daniel foretold much of it.

eras.name: Life of Jesus
eras.summary: The birth, ministry, death and resurrection of Jesus Christ.

eras.name: Early Church
eras.summary: Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, Paul's journeys across the Roman world, and the letters of the New Testament.
